title: Generic Fp prime FieldVec batch dispatch (Solinas-friendly)
description:
Extend the `SimdVecOps` SoA path with a generic Solinas-friendly Montgomery reducer so any prime fitting that form gets AVX2 batch dispatch instead of the scalar fallback. V0→V3 with mostly-existing scaffolding.

## Background

`gfp::FieldVec` add/sub/mul previously dispatched to AVX2 batch kernels only for `Fp<65537>` and `Fp<2^31-1>`. All other primes — including the 64-bit primes used by `gfpn` tower extensions — fell through to scalar element-wise loops in `crates/gf2-core/src/gfp/simd_ops.rs` and the callers in `gfpn/`.

The fix extends `SimdVecOps` with a guarded generic Montgomery reducer template (lazy reduction + final correction). Existing Mersenne and Fermat specialisations stay on their dedicated paths; eligible non-special primes can route through the new generic SIMD path before the scalar fallback.

PPC walk: V0 baseline (`fp_specialized` and `fieldvec_dot_product` benches with a non-Mersenne, non-Fermat prime, pinned by I1) → V3 generic SIMD reducer → asm verify.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] Existing Mersenne/Fermat specialisations remain bit-exact and at least as fast.
- [hard] Generic path bit-exact against scalar for every prime in the existing `proofs/` test suite.
- [hard] Word-boundary `#[test]`s for batch sizes $\in \{0, 1, 63, 64, 65, 127, 128, 129, 255, 256, 257\}$.
- [hard] Sibling `*.asm.txt` artefact regenerated.
- [hard] `perf stat -r 10` capture before/after recorded.
- [hard] Lean4 proofs still build (`./scripts/verify-lean.sh`).
- [aspirational] Empirical performance for non-special primes at the design batch size is recorded; the initial guarded dispatch is accepted without a 1.5× closure requirement because measured throughput is near parity or regressive and further speedup work belongs in follow-up PPC tasks.

## Amendment Notes

- The original aspirational target was $\geq 1.5\times$ geomean over scalar fallback for at least one non-special prime. Empirical evidence in `dev/benchmarks/cad241e6-criterion.txt` showed the near-M31 generic dispatch at about 1.05× versus the scalar loop and the near-M61 generic dispatch slower than scalar; the configured A3 `fieldvec_dot_fp_large` comparison also measured 1.000× geomean against the baseline artifacts. The hard contract remains guarded, bit-exact generic SIMD dispatch that does not hijack existing Fermat/Mersenne specialisations.

## Notes

Bench: `fp_specialized`, `fieldvec_dot_product` (existing, pinned by I1). Spec doc: `dev/plans/gf2_core_ppc_spiral.md`.
